answer: Intravenous alteplase, also known as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA), is recommended within 4.5 hours of symptom onset for eligible patients with acute ischemic stroke according to the AHA/ASA Acute Ischemic Stroke Guideline from 2021 [AHA/ASA Acute Ischemic Stroke Guideline, 2021]. This guideline provides evidence for the time window within which intravenous alteplase should be administered to patients experiencing acute ischemic stroke. It is important to note that patients who present with large vessel occlusion may also benefit from mechanical thrombectomy if treatment is initiated within a 24-hour window in selected cases. [AHA/ASA Acute Ischemic Stroke Guideline, 2021]

results.content: The F.A.S.T. warning signs of stroke are: Face drooping on one side, Arm weakness or drift when raised, Speech that is slurred or strange, and Time to call emergency services immediately if any of these signs appear, even if they resolve. Fast treatment significantly improves outcomes.
